questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.1 Identify overhead guard purpose and visibility requirements
questions.text: When is an overhead guard needed on a forklift?

answers.text: When the operator is exposed to hoisted or stacked objects that might fall
Whenever the operator wants to drive faster
Solely when the forklift is parked outdoors
When the forklift is used as a passenger vehicle

explanations.a: An overhead guard protects the operator from certain falling-object hazards when hoisted or stacked objects could fall. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: An overhead guard is a protective feature, not a speed-control device.
explanations.c: The need depends on falling-object exposure, not outdoor parking.
explanations.d: Forklifts are not intended for passenger transport.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.1 Identify overhead guard purpose and visibility requirements
questions.text: What should be true about overhead guard design?

answers.text: It should be removed when loads are tall
It must protect the operator while not interfering with good visibility
It should be used as a storage rack for tools
It should block the operator’s view to prevent distraction

explanations.a: Removing a protective guard can expose the operator to falling objects.
explanations.b: The workbook states guards must be constructed so they do not interfere with good visibility. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Storing tools on the guard can create falling-object hazards.
explanations.d: Blocking visibility can create collision and struck-by hazards.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.1 Identify overhead guard purpose and visibility requirements
questions.text: During forklift component inspection, what is a key requirement for openings in the top of an overhead guard?

answers.text: Openings should be cut larger when visibility is poor
Openings must be large enough for loose material to pass through
Openings must not exceed 6 inches in one of the two dimensions, width or length
Openings are unrestricted if the operator wears a hard hat

explanations.a: Changing guard openings can reduce protection and may be an unsafe modification.
explanations.b: Large openings can reduce falling-object protection.
explanations.c: The workbook identifies a 6-inch limit in one dimension for overhead guard openings. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: A hard hat does not replace overhead guard requirements.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.1 Identify overhead guard purpose and visibility requirements
questions.text: Why must an overhead guard extend over the operator under normal conditions, including forward tilt?

answers.text: So it can carry extra pallets above the operator
So operators can stand on it during maintenance
So it replaces the need for safe stacking
So the guard protects the operator during normal operating positions

explanations.a: The guard is not a load-carrying shelf.
explanations.b: The guard is not a work platform.
explanations.c: Loads still need to be secure and handled safely.
explanations.d: The guard must be large enough to extend over the operator during normal operation, including forward tilt. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.2 Identify load backrest purpose and requirements
questions.text: What characteristics should a load backrest have?

answers.text: A lightweight design that can bend away from the load
Large openings that allow small items through
Sufficient height, width, and strength to prevent the load from falling toward the operator
A removable design used only when convenient

explanations.a: A weak backrest may not stop material from falling toward the operator.
explanations.b: Openings must not allow load parts to fall toward the operator.
explanations.c: The workbook states the backrest must have enough height, width, and strength for this protective purpose. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Protection should be in place when the load creates the hazard.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.2 Identify load backrest purpose and requirements
questions.text: What is the visibility expectation for a load backrest?

answers.text: It should be removed whenever visibility is restricted
It should be used only as a decoration behind the mast
It should be opaque so operators cannot see the load
It must be constructed so it does not interfere with good visibility

explanations.a: Removal can expose the operator to falling-load hazards.
explanations.b: A load backrest is a safety component, not decoration.
explanations.c: Blocking visibility can create additional hazards.
explanations.d: The workbook says load backrests must not interfere with good visibility. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.2 Identify load backrest purpose and requirements
questions.text: A trainer is reviewing forklift protective features. What is the purpose of a vertical-load backrest?

answers.text: To help prevent a load or part of a load from falling toward the operator
To allow overloaded loads if they are stacked neatly
To increase travel speed with raised loads
To replace the forklift data plate

explanations.a: Load backrests protect the operator when handling small objects or unbanded units that could fall backward. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: A backrest does not increase rated capacity.
explanations.c: A backrest does not make high-speed travel safe.
explanations.d: The data plate still provides capacity and configuration information.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.2 Identify load backrest purpose and requirements
questions.text: When are forklifts required to have a vertical-load backrest in the workbook?

answers.text: When carrying workers on the forks
When handling small objects or unbanded units
Solely when operating on public highways
When the operator wants better rear visibility

explanations.a: Forks are not for carrying workers.
explanations.b: Forklifts that handle small objects or unbanded units need a backrest to help prevent material from falling toward the operator. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: The requirement relates to the type of load being handled.
explanations.d: Answer boundary: a load backrest protects from load movement; it does not improve rear visibility.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.3 Recognize shear-point guard purpose and examples
questions.text: During forklift component inspection, what hazard do shear-point guards address?

answers.text: Operator exposure to hazardous shear points such as mast chains or moving parts
Chemical vapor exposure from fuel
Noise from backup alarms
Loose paperwork in the operator compartment

explanations.a: Shear-point guards protect operators from hazardous exposure to chains, mast areas, and similar moving parts. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Shear guards protect against mechanical contact, not chemical exposure.
explanations.c: Answer boundary: noise control is not the purpose of a shear-point guard.
explanations.d: Paperwork is not the mechanical shear-point hazard described.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.3 Recognize shear-point guard purpose and examples
questions.text: Where might a protective barrier be needed on a forklift?

answers.text: Between the operator and every dashboard label
Between the operator and the mast if exposure to chains or shear points exists
Between pedestrians and the break room door
Between the operator and the seat belt buckle

explanations.a: Labels do not create shear-point exposure.
explanations.b: The workbook gives this as an example of guarding needed for hazardous shear-point exposure. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Pedestrian control is important, but it is not a shear-point guard location.
explanations.d: The seat belt buckle is not the mast shear-point hazard.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.3 Recognize shear-point guard purpose and examples
questions.text: Which condition should be corrected?

answers.text: A forklift inspected for moving-part exposure before use
A protective barrier that prevents contact with mast chains
An exposed chain or mast shear point that the operator could contact
A guard installed without blocking safe operation

explanations.a: Inspection helps identify whether guarding is needed.
explanations.b: A barrier helps control shear-point exposure.
explanations.c: Exposed moving parts can catch or shear body parts and should be guarded when hazardous exposure exists. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Guards should protect without creating new operational hazards.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.3 Recognize shear-point guard purpose and examples
questions.text: Which statement best addresses shear-point guards? Why should shear-point guards remain in place?

answers.text: They increase forklift rated capacity
They replace operator training
They make pedestrian lanes unnecessary
They help prevent contact with hazardous moving parts during operation

explanations.a: Shear guards do not increase load capacity.
explanations.b: Answer boundary: operators still need training on hazards and safe operation.
explanations.c: Pedestrian controls are separate from machine guarding.
explanations.d: Removing guards can expose the operator to moving chains or mast-related shear points. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.4 Recognize protective feature limitations and operator responsibilities
questions.text: On site, a trainer is reviewing forklift protective features. What is a limitation of a load backrest?

answers.text: It makes load weight irrelevant
It permits operators to exceed the data plate capacity
It helps prevent load parts from falling backward but does not make unstable loads safe
It eliminates the need to inspect the load

explanations.a: Answer boundary: load weight remains critical to capacity and stability.
explanations.b: The data plate capacity must still be followed.
explanations.c: A load backrest is one control and does not replace securing, balancing, and capacity checks. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Operators still need to evaluate load condition and security.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.4 Recognize protective feature limitations and operator responsibilities
questions.text: Which action is unsafe because it treats a protective feature as a substitute for safe work?

answers.text: Checking that a backrest is present for small unbanded loads
Avoiding contact with exposed mast moving parts
Keeping the load low while traveling
Driving under unstable stacked material because the forklift has an overhead guard

explanations.a: Checking the backrest supports safe operation.
explanations.b: Avoiding hazardous moving parts is safe practice.
explanations.c: Keeping loads low supports stability.
explanations.d: An overhead guard is not permission to enter falling-object hazards unnecessarily. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.4 Recognize protective feature limitations and operator responsibilities
questions.text: Which statement best describes forklift protective features?

answers.text: They reduce specific hazards but do not remove the need for safe operation
They eliminate pedestrian hazards around forklifts
They make overloads safe if the operator is careful
They allow travel with any load raised high

explanations.a: Protective features help control hazards, but operators still must follow safe practices. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Pedestrian separation and communication remain necessary.
explanations.c: Protective features do not override rated capacity.
explanations.d: Raised loads can still create stability and struck-by hazards.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.4 Recognize protective feature limitations and operator responsibilities
questions.text: What should an operator remember about overhead guards?

answers.text: They make seat restraints unnecessary during overturn hazards
They are not designed to protect against every possible falling object or tip-over injury
They allow workers to stand under elevated loads
They permit loads to be stacked loosely above the operator

explanations.a: Seat restraints remain important where overturn or ejection hazards exist.
explanations.b: Overhead guards provide limited falling-object protection and do not make unsafe operation acceptable. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: No one should stand under elevated portions or suspended hazards.
explanations.d: Loads must still be stable and secure.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.5 Apply component hazard recognition during inspection and operation
questions.text: During pre-use inspection, what should an operator check about safety components?

answers.text: Whether guards, backrests, plates, and decals are present, secure, and readable where applicable
Whether the forklift looks freshly painted
Whether the horn sounds pleasant
Whether the forklift is the fastest one available

explanations.a: Inspection should identify missing or damaged safety components and unreadable information. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Paint appearance does not prove safety components are usable.
explanations.c: The horn must work, but pleasant sound is not the safety criterion.
explanations.d: Speed is not the goal of inspection.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.5 Apply component hazard recognition during inspection and operation
questions.text: Which statement best addresses component inspection and operation? What should an operator do if a required guard is damaged or missing?

answers.text: Modify the guard personally without approval
Report the condition and remove the forklift from service if safe operation is affected
Ignore the damage if the shift is almost over
Continue operating because guards are optional decorations

explanations.a: Unauthorized modifications can create new hazards.
explanations.b: Damaged or missing protective features can create hazards and should be addressed before use. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Short remaining work time does not make damaged equipment safe.
explanations.d: Protective guards are safety features, not decorations.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.5 Apply component hazard recognition during inspection and operation
questions.text: Which operational choice supports protective component effectiveness?

answers.text: Use the backrest as a climbing step
Reach through the mast to adjust a moving load
Keep arms and legs inside the running lines and away from the mast
Lean outside the operator area while traveling

explanations.a: The backrest is not designed as a step or access point.
explanations.b: Reaching into mast areas can expose the operator to shear points.
explanations.c: The workbook instructs operators to keep arms and legs from the mast and within the running lines of the forklift. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Leaning out increases struck-by and crush exposure.

questions.name: Components and Protective Features
questions.objective: 2.5 Apply component hazard recognition during inspection and operation
questions.text: A forklift handles loose small boxes without a load backrest. What is the concern?

answers.text: The forklift will automatically stop moving
The forklift data plate becomes unnecessary
The forklift becomes approved for carrying passengers
Parts of the load could fall toward the operator

explanations.a: Missing a backrest does not create automatic stopping.
explanations.b: Data plates remain necessary for safe operation.
explanations.c: A missing backrest does not make passenger carrying acceptable.
explanations.d: Small or unbanded loads can fall backward toward the operator without an adequate backrest. This is the correct answer.
